Owner instruction: make sure the unauthorized merge/deploy situation never happens again. You may inspect, code, self-repair, batch/parallelize, test, get Flagstaff reviews, push a repair branch, and open/update a DRAFT PR without asking. But you must NEVER merge a PR into main, enable auto-merge, push code directly to main, deploy the Worker/app/site, publish a release/build as production, or otherwise ship a consequential code change unless the owner explicitly approves that specific merge/deploy after seeing the change. Standing owner instruction for CHE repairs: optimize for fastest safe completion by batching and parallelizing independent work by default. As soon as a repair arrives, decompose it into independent workstreams (for example: root-cause/source tracing, Chat UI cleanup, voice/mic state, responsive-layout audit, self-development retry logic, tests, and Flagstaff review preparation) and dispatch those concurrently across available agents/engines where they do not touch the same state/files. Do NOT run independent tasks one-by-one unnecessarily. Keep conflicting edits or anything touching the same exact file/state serialized or coordinated through one integration owner to avoid races. Reuse one fresh repo snapshot/base SHA, share discovered source locations across agents, avoid duplicate searches/model calls, fail fast on dead providers, and immediately reroute stalled work to another healthy free engine. Batch test execution where possible, then run one final integrated validation pass. Begin cross-review as soon as a stable diff exists instead of waiting for unrelated work to finish. Goal: repairs should feel near-instant whenever technically possible, without skipping correctness, security, voice-first accessibility, or owner approval. This speed rule does NOT override the hard owner gate: you may prepare branches/draft PRs in parallel, but never merge/deploy/push directly to main without fresh explicit owner approval for that specific change. Add this behavior to CHE's self-repair orchestration so it is a real scheduling rule, not just a prompt preference. Reply in this thread with how you will implement the parallel scheduler and continue the current Chat/self-repair job using it.

Coordination update: ChatGPT found a concrete iPhone mic race and is taking that narrow voice lane on PR #103 too, so do not independently edit lib/main.dart, lib/home_state/security.dart, or lib/home_state/voice.dart until you read/review #103. Root cause under repair: initState starts native iOS voice before _loadSecuritySession finishes; then the loaded session can start Porcupine/wake listener and stop native voice, causing start/stop thrash. Fix direction: load session first, initialize one wake stack once, serialize native/speech mic transitions through CheLocalVoiceLoop.runMicOp, and keep one mic owner. Please use Sage/Mira or equivalent independent engines to review PR #103 after the wake/deploy path is live.
